key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the constituents and their addition sequence: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide provides surface passivation.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor chemistry and mixing order could help preserve MXenes during perovskite solar-cell fabrication.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Use X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to track surface chemical changes.
Apply density functional theory to investigate surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS and DFT findings indicate rapid degradation with iodine/polyiodides, slower oxidation with PbI2, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization with MAI.
watch_item: The abstract reports precursor-level chemistry, not device-efficiency or operational-lifetime validation; addition sequence requires careful control.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
